title: The Russell Reconstitution Effect
one_line: Russell index reconstitutions (1996-2001) produced economically and statistically significant abnormal returns from temporary price pressure and permanent liquidity changes, with very high volatility on reconstitution day; later work finds the effect and its reversals weakening.

findings.statement: Significant abnormal returns around June reconstitution, 1996-2001.
Additions gain on the reconstitution date rather than the announcement; deletions negative.
Effect and reversals much smaller in recent years.

reported_results.headline: Russell index reconstitutions (1996-2001) produced economically and statistically significant abnormal returns from temporary price pressure and permanent liquidity changes, with very high volatility on reconstitution day; later work finds the effect and its reversals weakening.

tradable_edge: Stock-level. Index angle: reconstitution day (late June) brings huge closing volume — note as an event day for ES/NQ close strategies.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read via a review of index-rebalancing studies; magnitudes not given there.
